description: Tamil Nadu is training postgraduate teachers in government high and higher secondary schools to use Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to create digital teaching resources, including animated videos, audio clips, images, songs and interactive puzzle games, as part of efforts to integrate AI into everyday classroom instruction.The training programme, being conducted by the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT), aims to help teachers simplify complex concepts and make classroom learning more interactive. In the first phase, postgraduate teachers of Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics are being trained through district-level sessions, which are expected to conclude by the end of October 2026.Teachers are expected to begin using AI-generated learning materials in classrooms from November, while educators teaching other subjects will be covered in subsequent phases, according to a report published in Dinamalar on October 28.Tamil Nadu Shifts From State-Made Videos To Teacher-Created ContentThe initiative marks a shift from the state's existing ICT-based teaching model, under which a state-level team developed dedicated videos for individual lessons and shared them with government schools over the past four years.Under the new approach, teachers will be trained to create their own subject-specific digital content using AI tools, including Google's video tools, NotebookLM, Claude and ChatGPT. The resources will include animated videos, audio material, images, songs and simple educational games tailored to classroom requirements.By the end of the training, each participating teacher is expected to develop AI-generated video content that can be incorporated into classroom instruction.AI To Support Concept-Based Learning In Government SchoolsAccording to programme coordinators, integrating AI into teaching can help educators explain difficult concepts through visual and interactive methods. Science topics such as force, energy and distance, along with mathematical concepts, can be presented through animations to improve students' understanding.The initiative also gives teachers greater flexibility to develop learning resources suited to their teaching methods and students' learning needs, rather than depending entirely on centrally produced instructional videos.The programme's implementation will depend on how effectively teachers can integrate these resources into regular classroom teaching. Access to devices and internet connectivity, along with guidance on content accuracy and the responsible use of generative AI tools, will remain important as the training expands to teachers of other subjects.
